steps.label: What is a research proposal?
desc: The aim of the research proposal is to present your proposed research clearly and concisely so that institutions can assess whether they will be able to supervise your research, or—for undergraduates—to show that you have carefully planned the research project for your dissertation.

steps.label: What are the core sections?
desc: It is essential for you to show that you understand the field and the focus of your research. The core sections of the research proposal are (1) the literature review, (2) the aims or research questions, and (3) the data and methodology. You will also need to include (4) limitations and (5) contribution of the study. Each of these sections will shed light on how your research will make an original contribution to the field.

steps.label: How is it structured?
desc: You can use this suggested outline to structure your research proposal.

steps.label: Look at the Introduction
desc: The model text is from the field of Human Resources Management and shows the structure and aims of each section of a research proposal.
Note that the model does not show the preliminary title, table of contents or full bibliography.
The Introduction introduces the reader to the current state of knowledge in the field. It provides definitions, summarizes key research and links these to the purposes of the research.

steps.label: Look at the Literature Review
desc: This section demonstrates the writer's understanding of the current literature and displays the ability to critically evaluate the cited sources.
It shows that the proposed research will be an original contribution to the field.

filters.label: The past tense is used to refer to cited research.

steps.label: Look at Purpose
desc: This section lists the aims of your study, using numbers.

filters.label: It makes use of research verbs.

steps.label: Look at Methods
desc: This section clarifies the proposed methodological approach and the data collection procedures.
It situates the proposed methodology within other research.

filters.label: The future tense is used to refer to the proposed method.

steps.label: Look at Limitations
desc: This section highlights limitations, showing awareness of the challenges of the research. It proposes possible solutions.

filters.label: Modal verbs are used to suggest limitations.

steps.label: Look at Contributions
desc: This section emphasizes the originality of the research and lists possible contributions of the research.

filters.label: Modal verbs are used to hedge contributions.
Phrases with ‘this study’ or ‘this research’ identify and link different aspects of the discussion to the current study.
Phrases using words such as ‘lack’ show the research gap and point to the originality of this study.
Use of the personal pronoun ‘I’ to take ownership of the study.
The research proposal uses a combination of tenses and modal verbs.

checkList.text:
Preparing for your study
Start thinking about your research topic in plenty of time.
Define your research questions.

Literature
As you read the relevant literature, read critically, take notes and remember to record bibliographic data (title, author, date, publisher and page numbers) for every source you read.

Draft
Organize your notes into the necessary sections of the proposal and write your draft. Use the model to help you. Write concisely and avoid repetition.
Revise and edit your draft.
Provide a statement of how you will access resources and acquire skills, such as using statistical software, if asked to do so.
